children: said on Wednesday it had received a fourth, improved offer from private equity firm Warburg Pincus, valuing the property developer at A$2.24 billion ($1.55 billion).
The improved bid of A$5.50 apiece represents a 50.7% premium to Ingenia's last closing price before Warburg Pincus' first bid in early September.

Warburg Pincus' third revised offer, comprising A$5.45 cash per share plus a permitted distribution of up to A$0.05 per share, is 1.9% or A$0.10 per share higher than AVID Property Group's offer announced on Monday.
The US-based firm also intends to bring in Australian Retirement Trust-backed Discovery Parks and LDR Capital, a unit of the Lederer family office, as co-investors.
Under the new proposal, Discovery Parks is expected to acquire Ingenia's holiday parks business, while LDR Capital could buy the property developer's gardens business.
Warburg Pincus' latest offer is subject, among other conditions, to Ingenia approving the participation of the two co-investors and their proposed acquisitions.
